quote: The bowls are built on a soy-sauce (shoyu) tare, including a dark-soy 'black' version; standard Japanese shoyu is brewed with wheat.
found: Own menu page, 背脂ブラック: 「完全オリジナルで厳選したたまり醤油に、じっくり仕込んだチャーシューの旨みを移した特製醤油を重ね合わせた、コク深い黒いスープが特徴の京都ラーメンです。」 Header line: 「アッキー流 中華そば — たまり醤油を使ったコクと旨みあるこだわりの味」
method: 1 plain fetch of the shop's own site (the cited URL)
note: IMPORTANT WORDING FIX. The shop does not say 'standard shoyu' — it says たまり醤油, twice, as its selling point. English-speaking celiacs are taught 'tamari = gluten-free', which is a US health-food convention; Japanese JAS たまり醤油 is a low-wheat soy sauce that usually still contains some wheat and is never certified GF. The record must name たまり醤油 explicitly and say it is NOT a gluten-free soy sauce, or a reader will do the substitution themselves. gf_confidence:no is unaffected — both bowls are wheat 中華そば noodles and the curry uses wheat roux.
